name: application-partial-failure-summary
title: Partial Failure Summary
description: Batch-operation result banner showing a computed N-of-total success rate and failure count, with an expandable list of per-item failure reasons — not present elsewhere in the registry; distinct from a plain error banner because it summarizes a mixed-outcome batch rather than a single failure.
useWhen: Reporting the outcome of a bulk operation (import, batch update, mass send) that partially failed.
You want the success rate computed live from real succeeded/failed counts.
Users need to see specific per-item failure reasons without the summary taking up permanent space.
avoidWhen: The operation either fully succeeded or fully failed — a simple success/error banner is sufficient.
There are no per-item error details to show — a plain count is enough.
You need this to auto-dismiss like a toast — use a persistent banner pattern instead since batch results need review time.
responsiveBehavior: The banner is fluid up to a max width; the summary text wraps naturally and the error list scrolls with the page rather than the component.
accessibility: Built on native <details>/<summary> so it's keyboard-operable and exposes expanded/collapsed state to assistive tech without extra ARIA wiring.
The success rate is stated as both a fraction (N of total) and a percentage in the same sentence, not just one or the other.
Each error row pairs the failing item identifier with its specific reason, not a generic 'failed' label.

variants.title: Partial failure summary
variants.description: A CSV import batch with 47 of 50 rows succeeding (94%) and 3 failing, expanded to show each row's specific error reason, on a light surface.
accessibility: Success rate percentage is computed from succeeded/(succeeded+failed), never a hand-typed number.

variants.title: Partial failure summary (Dark)
variants.description: The same 47-of-50 batch result, adapted for dark surfaces.
accessibility: Amber text and border colors meet WCAG AA contrast on dark backgrounds.
